text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your current symptoms of right knee pain and swelling, and tell me more about the history of your left ankle and any urinary issues you've experienced.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome)

Your history of urethritis (pain with urination), current monoarthritis (right knee), and a preceding oligoarthritis (left ankle) is the classic triad of Reiter's Syndrome, also known as Reactive Arthritis. The onset of symptoms 1-3 weeks after a potential genitourinary infection, combined with your sexual history, strongly supports this diagnosis. I have already noted your mother's history of rheumatoid arthritis; however, your presentation is distinct from that autoimmune condition. To confirm the diagnosis, I will need to see the results of a Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and a Joint_Aspiration from your right knee to rule out septic arthritis and identify any specific pathogens.
